content.p: Lightning is a static blogging engine designed to make it painless to author and update large blogs. Key features are:

ul.li: Use your favorite editor for everything.

content.p: Here's a preview of how easy it is to use lightning blogging flow screencast once you're set up.

ol.li: Clone the repository via git clone git@github.com:borismus/lightning.git
Run cd lightning to get to your newly cloned repository.
Install all required dependencies by running pip install -r requirements.txt.
Run ./lightning to build and ./lightning preview to run a webserver.

content.p: Forcibly rebuild everything regardless of whether or not there have been changes made to the content. This is useful if you change your template.
Start watching for local changes to the content, rebuilding incrementally based on that.
Start a really simple local web server with its document root pointing to the output directory.

ol.li: lightning.yaml specifies where to look for content, template and where to dump output.
site.yaml in your content directory specifies site-specific configuration.

content.p: I use a combination of Dropbox and Lightning (which uses inotify-tools) to make for a pleasant blogging experience. Here are the steps to get Lightning working on your server.

ol.li: Install Lightning on your server (see above).
Configure lightning.yaml to look for your content on Dropbox (eg. ~/Dropbox/my-blog/)
Setup a watcher on your server via lightning watch.
Make some changes to your content directory from any Dropbox client (I sometimes use Nebulous on iPad).

content.p: This is Lightning, yet another static blogging engine!
